from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors act as instructions in space.", "We can scale these vectors.", "We can add vectors together."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Vector as an Instruction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5, 1], y_range=[-1, 5, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        vec = Vector([2, 3], color="#FFD700")
        vec.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.add(vec)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")
        scaled_vec = Vector([4, 6], color="#32CD32")
        scaled_vec.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.play(FadeIn(scaled_vec), run_time=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF1493")
        vec_add = Vector([2, 3], color="#FF1493")
        vec_add.shift(axes.c2p(2, 3))
        self.play(Create(vec_add), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations and Span", ["Linear combinations combine scaled vectors.", "Span is all reachable points.", "Different directions cover the plane."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 1. Display two basis vectors on the plane. Color: #FFD700 (Gold).
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT + UP, color="#FFD700")
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.5 + DOWN, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'D3')
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # 2. Draw linear combination as path of two vectors. Color: #00BFFF (Deep Sky Blue).
        path = VGroup(v1.copy(), v2.copy().shift(v1.get_end()))
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        
        # 3. Highlight resulting grid points. Color: #FF4500 (Orange Red).
        dot = Dot(path[1].get_end(), color="#FF4500")
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        # 4. Fill the span area with light shading. Color: #32CD32 (Lime Green).
        span_area = Polygon(
            np.array([-3, -3, 0]), np.array([3, -3, 0]),
            np.array([3, 3, 0]), np.array([-3, 3, 0]),
            color="#32CD32", fill_opacity=0.2
        )
        self.place_in_area(span_area, 'A1', 'F6')
        self.play(FadeIn(span_area))
        
        # 5. Show scaling basis vectors to fill plane. Color: #FF1493 (Deep Pink).
        self.play(v1.animate.scale(1.5), v2.animate.scale(1.5))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF1493")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector", ["Redundant vectors add no information.", "They lie on the same span.", "Dependence means lost dimensionality."])
        
        # Create vectors
        v1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        v2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=WHITE)
        v3 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=(RIGHT+UP)*1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Position them
        group = VGroup(v1, v2, v3)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'B2', 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        # Highlight that v3 lies on span of v1 and v2 (linear combination)
        self.play(Indicate(v3))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(FadeOut(v3))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Bases: The Minimalist Framework", [
            "A basis spans the space.", 
            "Vectors must be linearly independent.", 
            "It is a minimal set.", 
            "Basis defines our coordinate system.", 
            "Basis points are always unique."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display two linearly independent vectors. Color: #FFD700
        v1 = Vector([1, 0.5], color="#FFD700")
        v2 = Vector([-0.5, 1], color="#FFD700")
        v_group = VGroup(v1, v2)
        self.place_at_grid(v_group, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Grid formed by these basis vectors. Color: #00BFFF
        axes = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#00BFFF", "stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(axes))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show how any point is reachable. Color: #FF4500
        point = Dot(color="#FF4500")
        point.move_to(axes.c2p(1.5, 2))
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        
        # Keep things on screen for a bit
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Spans represent all possible reaches.",
            "Basis defines a minimal framework.",
            "Independence prevents redundant information.",
            "Redundancy collapses our total span.",
            "Summary: Basis describes space efficiently."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Summary", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup for vectors
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)
        
        v1 = Vector([2, 1], color=YELLOW)
        v2 = Vector([-1, 2], color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1, 2 & 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), 
                  self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        v3 = Vector([1, 0.5], color=BLUE) # Redundant to v1
        self.play(Create(v3))
        self.play(v1.animate.set_opacity(0.3), v3.animate.set_opacity(0.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(FadeOut(v3), v1.animate.set_opacity(1.0))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Spans to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector as an Instruction
sections.content: Define a vector as an arrow in 2D space. Introduce the concept of 'scaling' and 'adding' vectors as movement instructions on a grid.
sections.example: A robot arm moving 2 units right (vector i) and 3 units up (vector j) to reach a coordinate (2,3).

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Explain that a linear combination is the result of scaling and adding vectors. The 'Span' is the set of all reachable points in space using these vectors.
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors as 'drawing tools'; if they point in different directions, their span covers the entire 2D plane (like painting a wall).

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
sections.content: Introduce linear dependence: if one vector lies on the span of the others, it provides no new information. Visually, this is a vector that lies on the same line as another.
sections.example: Two squirrels running in the same direction; the second squirrel is redundant because it doesn't help the group reach any new territory.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimalist Framework
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that is both linearly independent and spans the entire space. It is the 'minimal set' of instructions needed to describe every point in the space.
sections.example: Using standard basis vectors (1,0) and (0,1) as a GPS coordinate system; you need exactly these two to uniquely identify any location on a map.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Connect the concepts: Linear combinations form the span. If vectors are independent, they form a basis. If dependent, they contain redundant information.
sections.example: A summary animation showing a 2D plane shrinking to a line (dependence) and expanding back to a plane when a new, independent vector is added.
